shared_elements: low-relief carved figures on a flat stone surface
bands/rows of repeated parallel incised lines (feather- or fringe-like patterning)
wing or bird-related motif (birds in profile in A, feathered wings in B)
justification: The only real correspondence is generic: both surfaces carry low-relief figural imagery with zones of repeated parallel incised lines, and both involve avian/wing forms (small profile birds stacked in registers in A, the great feathered wings of a single figure in B). Otherwise the content differs fundamentally: A is a stacked sequence of small schematic animals (birds, a quadruped, elongated serpentine forms) with no dominant actor, while B is a single large, densely detailed anthropomorphic winged being with fringed garment and a rosette, an iconography absent from A.
